newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe bunkers little changed, only Hamburg active.
newsitem.headline: Europe bunkers little changed, only Hamburg active.

text.p: European bunker prices were mixed, but little changed on Monday, with Hamburg the only port registering reasonable volumes, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 CST was only $1 a tonne up, despite a fuel oil barge market $3 higher. Bunkers traded early at $127 and then at $128 fob.
Traded volume was poor and suppliers said the lack of buying interest was part of the reason that prices only rose slightly.
Hamburg prices were also up by $1 a tonne as demand improved. After a week watching other ports picking up business, volumes were significantly higher.
"We saw 15,000 tonnes today and (prices) then rose. I guess people have been holding off for a while," one supplier said.
Prices in Mediterranean ports varied by about $1 from Friday's closing levels. Traded volumes were minimal.
Spanish ports lifted their prices by $1 a tonne, France was steady, but Piraeus came down by $1.
Fujairah bunkers were about $1 a tonne firmer, supported by Singapore levels.
South African bunkers were down as immediate supply problems eased. Fuel oil 180 CST was at $127/$129 ex wharf.
